verdict_reason: THE SCORING KERNEL IS THE REFERENCE'S KERNEL, BUT THE CHAIN IT IS FED IS NOT. I cloned Alsace08/Chain-of-Embedding and read how the released code builds the chain: `inference.py::print_hidden_states` takes `generation_output.hidden_states` and loops `for j in range(layer_num)` where `layer_num = len(hidden_states[1])` -- i.e. THE RAW HF TUPLE, all L+1 entries INCLUDING the final `ln_f(...)`, with no hook and no trim. BLME substitutes the deepest block's raw pre-norm output (`_hs[-1] = _h`, `_meta_last_entry_is_block_output` True on every model). Feeding both chains to BLME's OWN `_coe_from_chain` on the same 100 WikiText passages, the headline coe_r CHANGES SIGN on all three models tested: gpt2 +0.013202 (reference chain) vs -0.183024 (BLME), pythia-70m -0.365734 vs +0.135602, distilgpt2 +0.120925 vs -0.214348; coe_c moves -56.3% / +222.1% / -57.1%. This is the same class of divergence that made `geometry_matrix_entropy` RED and `geometry_contextualization` YELLOW last round, and it is larger. YELLOW, not RED, because the paper's Eq. 3 defines the chain over the hidden states of the layers and a raw block output is a defensible reading of that -- but a reader must be told the sign of the headline flips relative to the released code.
comparable_reason: Ang~ is a 1/L average by construction and `mean_normalized_angle` carries rho -0.657 with n_layers and -0.556 with d_model over 16 models; `mean_angle_change` -0.646 / -0.494. `coe_r` itself is near-neutral (rho +0.189 d_model, +0.063 n_layers) but heavy-tailed: over 16 models it spans -0.324 to +2.286 with fourteen models inside [-0.33, +0.24], so any linear model on it is fitted by one point. `_meta_chain_length_per_sample` equals n_layers exactly and is correctly prefixed.
normalized_variant: _meta_normalized_coe_c (a literal alias of coe_c; correctly demoted)

THE DEMOTION DID NOT REMOVE THE COLLINEARITY IT WAS FOR. The file's comment now claims 'coe_r, coe_c and mean_normalized_angle span the same space with no linear dependency between them'. Measured over 16 models that is false: coe_c vs (coe_r + mean_normalized_angle) has pearson 0.9999269947745999 (max |residual| 0.1307, max rel 6.9%). The identity coe_r == mag - ang is confirmed exact (max |residual| 2.50e-16), and coe_c is pearson 0.99993 with the demoted mag -- so demoting mag moved one degree of freedom out of the matrix and left another, near-identical one (coe_c) in, alongside both of its components.

A SECOND NEAR-DUPLICATE PAIR, both feature-eligible: pearson(coe_c_std, coe_r_std) = 0.9979 over 16 models. Also pearson(mean_angle_change, mean_normalized_angle) = 0.9880 and pearson(mean_magnitude_change, std_magnitude_change) = 0.9877.
